title: Ancient Rome: Culture and Society
text: Roman culture was shaped by a blend of native Italian traditions and influences from conquered peoples, especially the Greeks. Roman society was divided into distinct classes: patricians (aristocracy), plebeians (commoners), and slaves, who constituted a significant portion of the population. The Roman family (familia) was the basic social unit, headed by the paterfamilias. Romans excelled in law, engineering, and military organization. Latin literature flourished with writers like Virgil, Ovid, Horace, and Cicero. Roman religion initially centered on a pantheon of gods adapted from Greek mythology. Architecture including the Colosseum, the Pantheon, and aqueducts demonstrated remarkable engineering sophistication.
